title: Perfect stress and particle balances with entropy identity

items.title: Perfect stress and particle balances with entropy identity
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$ be a smooth time-oriented Lorentzian four-manifold of signature
$(-,+,+,+)$, let $\nabla$ be its metric-compatible torsion-free connection, and
let $u$ be a smooth future-directed vector field with $g(u,u)=-1$. Put
$\Delta^{ab}=g^{ab}+u^au^b$, $D=u^a\nabla_a$, $\theta=\nabla_a u^a$,
$a^b=u^a\nabla_a u^b$, and $\Delta^b{}_a=\delta^b{}_a+u^bu_a$.
Take a smooth fixed-composition state from [[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]] with
$n>0$, $T>0$, $s=n\sigma_p$, and $h=\epsilon+p=Ts+\mu n$ as in
[[lem-tgr-local-gibbs-euler]]. Define the perfect stress tensor and particle
current by

$$T^{ab}=\epsilon u^a u^b+p\Delta^{ab},\qquad J^a=nu^a.$$

For any smooth vector field $f^b$, the balance equation $\nabla_aT^{ab}=f^b$
is equivalent to the pair

$$D\epsilon+h\theta=-u_bf^b,\qquad ha^c+\Delta^{ca}\nabla_a p=\Delta^c{}_bf^b,$$

and $\nabla_aJ^a=0$ is equivalent to $Dn+n\theta=0$. Whenever both balances
hold, the exact entropy identities are

$$T\nabla_a(su^a)=-u_bf^b,\qquad nT D\sigma_p=-u_bf^b.$$

In particular, when $f=0$, the entropy current $su$ is divergence-free and
specific entropy is advected, $D\sigma_p=0$. These are conditional identities
for supplied smooth fields; they assert no solution existence or physical
applicability beyond the stated model data.

references.title: Eric Gourgoulhon, An Introduction to Relativistic Hydrodynamics, arXiv:gr-qc/0603009v1
references.locator: PDF pp. 16–20, §4.3 and §§5.2–5.4: local Gibbs variables, perfect stress divergence, parallel and orthogonal projections.

references.title: Paul Romatschke, Relativistic Viscous Fluid Dynamics and Non-Equilibrium Entropy, arXiv:0906.4787v2
references.locator: PDF pp. 7–8, §3: stress decomposition and the Landau/Eckart frame distinction; the local balance proof here is independent.

items.title: Enthalpy vorticity and restricted material circulation
items.statement:
Use the state, signature, connection, and perfect-fluid data of
[[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]] and [[lem-tgr-perfect-fluid-projection]], with
$f=0$, $n>0$, and $T>0$. Put $v=1/n$, $H=(\epsilon+p)/n=e+pv$, and let
$c>0$ be the fixed speed-of-light normalization in the convention $x^0=ct$.
For the momentum one-form $P=(H/c)u^\flat$, consider a smooth closed curve
$\gamma_0:[0,1]\to M$ with equal endpoint values and a local flow
$\Phi_\lambda$ of $u$ defined on a neighborhood of its compact image. Write
$\gamma_\lambda=\Phi_\lambda\circ\gamma_0$ and
$\mathcal C(\lambda)=\int_{\gamma_\lambda}P$. Then

$$\iota_u d(Hu^\flat)=T\,d\sigma_p,\qquad \frac{d\mathcal C}{d\lambda}=\frac1c\int_{\gamma_\lambda}T\,d\sigma_p.$$

Consequently, circulation is conserved if $\sigma_p$ is constant on the
region swept out by the loop. The local identity does not assert circulation
conservation merely from $D\sigma_p=0$, nor does it assume a global flow,
complete spacetime, or shock solution.

references.title: Eric Gourgoulhon, An Introduction to Relativistic Hydrodynamics, arXiv:gr-qc/0603009v1
references.locator: PDF pp. 20–24, §§6.1–6.3: Carter–Lichnerowicz identity, entropy per baryon, and restricted isentropic circulation.

references.title: Paul Romatschke, Relativistic Viscous Fluid Dynamics and Non-Equilibrium Entropy, arXiv:0906.4787v2
references.locator: PDF pp. 7–8, §3: relativistic stress and frame conventions; circulation is derived locally here.

items.title: Frame-qualified dissipative entropy cancellation
items.statement:
Let $(M,g,N)$, $u$, $\nabla$, and the fixed-composition state be as in
[[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]] and [[lem-tgr-local-gibbs-euler]], with
$g(u,u)=-1$, $n>0$, and $T>0$. Define
$\Delta^{ab}=g^{ab}+u^au^b$, $\Delta_{ab}=g_{ab}+u_au_b$,
$\Delta_a{}^b=\delta_a{}^b+u_au^b$, and $D=u^a\nabla_a$,
$\theta=\nabla_a u^a$, $a^b=u^a\nabla_a u^b$, and the spatial symmetric
trace-free shear

$$\sigma_{ab}=\Delta_a{}^c\Delta_b{}^d\nabla_{(c}u_{d)} -\frac{\theta}{3}\Delta_{ab},$$

where parentheses denote the averaged symmetric part. Suppose smooth fields
$\Pi$, $Q^a$, $V^a$, and $\pi^{ab}$ obey $u_aQ^a=u_aV^a=0$,
$u_a\pi^{ab}=0$, and $\pi^{ab}$ is symmetric with $g_{ab}\pi^{ab}=0$. Set

$$T^{ab}=\epsilon u^au^b+(p+\Pi)\Delta^{ab} +u^aQ^b+Q^au^b+\pi^{ab},\qquad J^a=nu^a+V^a.$$

If $\nabla_aT^{ab}=f^b$ and $\nabla_aJ^a=0$, the vector field

$$S^a=su^a+\frac{Q^a}{T}-\frac{\mu V^a}{T}$$

satisfies the exact identity

$$\nabla_aS^a=-\frac{\Pi\theta+\pi^{ab}\sigma_{ab}}{T} -\frac{Q^a(\nabla_aT+Ta_a)}{T^2} -V^a\nabla_a\!\left(\frac{\mu}{T}\right)-\frac{u_bf^b}{T}.$$

This identity applies to the stated smooth fields and conventions; it does not
select a constitutive law or assert that any such fields solve an evolution
problem.

references.title: Eric Gourgoulhon, An Introduction to Relativistic Hydrodynamics, arXiv:gr-qc/0603009v1
references.locator: PDF pp. 16–20, §§4.3 and 5.2–5.4: local Gibbs identity and the perfect-stress energy projection used as the baseline.

references.title: Paul Romatschke, Relativistic Viscous Fluid Dynamics and Non-Equilibrium Entropy, arXiv:0906.4787v2
references.locator: PDF pp. 7–13, §§3–4.1: dissipative stress decomposition and entropy-current divergence for its stated conformal, zero-charge scope.

items.title: Positive first-order residual and actual instability/tail counterexamples
items.statement:
Use the smooth state, frame, and dissipative stress/particle decomposition of
[[def-tgr-local-fluid-state]] and [[lem-tgr-dissipative-entropy-identity]].
Assume the stress and particle balances $\nabla_aT^{ab}=f^b$ and
$\nabla_aJ^a=0$. Let $c>0$, $T>0$, and let $\eta,\zeta,\kappa,L\ge0$. Impose

$$\Pi=-\zeta c\theta,\quad \pi^{ab}=-2\eta c\sigma^{ab},\quad Q^a=-\frac{\kappa}{c}\Delta^{ab}(\nabla_bT+Ta_b),\quad V^a=-L\Delta^{ab}\nabla_b(\mu/T).$$

On any branch with no rest-frame work, $u_bf^b=0$ (including the isolated case
$f^b=0$), the entropy identity reduces to

$$\nabla_aS^a= \frac{\zeta c\theta^2+2\eta c\,\sigma^{ab}\sigma_{ab}}{T} +\frac{\kappa}{cT^2}\Delta^{ab}(\nabla_aT+Ta_a)(\nabla_bT+Ta_b) +L\Delta^{ab}\nabla_a(\mu/T)\nabla_b(\mu/T)\ge0.$$

This sign condition alone implies neither finite propagation nor linear
stability, as the following two conditional model calculations show.

1. **Supported fixed-rest Fourier branch.** Let $M=\mathbb R^4$ have Minkowski
metric $g=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$, choose $N=(1,0,0,0)$ as time
orientation, and write $x^0=ct$. On the positive-time field domain
$O=\{(x^0,\mathbf x):x^0>0,\ \mathbf x\in\mathbb R^3\}$ set
$u=(1,0,0,0)$. Set $V=\Pi=\pi=0$ and $\eta=\zeta=L=0$, and maintain the
fixed rest field with external support
$f^0=0$, $f^i=\partial_i p+c^{-1}\partial_tQ^i$, hence $u_bf^b=0$ even if
$f^i$ is nonzero. On a fixed-volume state slice
$v=v_0$, let $T=T_0+\vartheta$ and
$\epsilon=\epsilon_0+C\vartheta$, where $T_0,C>0$ are constant and the
temperature coordinate is valid on an interval $[T_0,T_0+\delta]$ contained in
the material-state domain for some $\delta>0$. With constant $\kappa>0$, set
$q=cQ=-\kappa\nabla\vartheta$. For any
$\vartheta_0\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ satisfying
$0\le\vartheta_0\le\delta$ and $\vartheta_0\not\equiv0$, the heat solution
$\vartheta(\mathbf x,t):=\int_{\mathbb R^3}\Gamma(\mathbf x-\mathbf y,\kappa t/C)
\vartheta_0(\mathbf y)\,d\mathbf y$ for $t>0$ has initial boundary trace
$\vartheta_0$ locally uniformly as $t\downarrow0^+$ and is strictly positive
at every $\mathbf x\in\mathbb R^3$ for every $t>0$. Hence no finite speed $v$ satisfies
$\operatorname{supp}\vartheta(\cdot,t)\subseteq
\operatorname{supp}\vartheta_0+\overline B_{vt}(0)$ for all $t>0$.

2. **Homogeneous Eckart linearization.** On the same Minkowski spacetime take
$f=0$ and a homogeneous rest state with $n_0,T_0>0$,
$h_0=\epsilon_0+p_0>0$, and $\kappa>0$. Set the density and temperature
perturbations to zero, $\delta n=\delta T=0$, take $V=0$, and impose no spatial
gradients. Let $\mathbf w:(0,\infty)\to\mathbb R^3$ be the first-order spatial
perturbation of $u$. The linearized first-order heat and momentum equations are
$Q^i=-(\kappa T_0/c^2)\dot w^i$ and
$h_0\dot{\mathbf w}+\dot{\mathbf Q}=0$. Hence for
$\lambda=h_0c^2/(\kappa T_0)>0$, every nonzero constant vector $\mathbf w_*$ gives
the growing linearized mode $\mathbf w(t)=\mathbf w_*e^{\lambda t}$.
This is a statement about the linearized equations, not a nonlinear solution
claim.

The results are conditional mathematical deductions from the displayed model
equations. They do not establish a constitutive law for nature, a nonlinear
existence theorem, or a general instability theorem.

references.title: Eric Gourgoulhon, An Introduction to Relativistic Hydrodynamics, arXiv:gr-qc/0603009v1
references.locator: PDF pp. 16–20, §§4.3 and 5.2–5.4: perfect-fluid state and balance conventions; the dissipative examples here are proved locally.

references.title: Paul Romatschke, Relativistic Viscous Fluid Dynamics and Non-Equilibrium Entropy, arXiv:0906.4787v2
references.locator: PDF pp. 7–13, §§3–4.1: first-order viscous constitutive context and an entropy-current analysis for a conformal zero-charge model; the tail and Eckart-mode arguments here are independent.

title: Perfect stress and particle balances with entropy identity — Examples

items.title: Null tensor has no timelike Landau frame
items.statement:
Take $M=\mathbb R^4$ with Minkowski metric
$g=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$ and choose the time orientation
$N=(1,0,0,0)$. By [[def-gr-smooth-lorentzian-objects]], a nonzero causal vector
$v$ is future-directed exactly when $g(v,N)<0$, which here is equivalent to
$v^0>0$. Let $\ell=(1,1,0,0)$, so $g(\ell,\ell)=0$ and
$g(\ell,N)=-1<0$; thus $\ell$ is future-directed null. Let $\rho>0$ and
define the symmetric tensor $T^{ab}=\rho\,\ell^a\ell^b$. A **Landau frame** for this
tensor means a future unit timelike vector $u$ for which the projected energy
flux $Q^a=-\Delta^a{}_cT^{cd}u_d$ vanishes. The current frame convention of
[[lem-tgr-fluid-frame-projection]] gives the unique stress decomposition; when
$Q=0$, contracting it with $u_b$ gives
$$T^a{}_bu^b=-\epsilon_u u^a,\qquad \epsilon_u=T^{ab}u_a u_b.$$
This explicit tensor has no Landau frame.

references.title: Eric Gourgoulhon, An Introduction to Relativistic Hydrodynamics, arXiv:gr-qc/0603009v1
references.locator: PDF pp. 16–20, §§4.3 and 5.2–5.4: perfect-stress and observer-frame conventions; the null-dust calculation here is local.

references.title: Paul Romatschke, Relativistic Viscous Fluid Dynamics and Non-Equilibrium Entropy, arXiv:0906.4787v2
references.locator: PDF p. 7, §3: Landau and Eckart frame definitions; its printed Landau sign is not used.
